 This Writ Petition Is Coming On For Preliminary
Hearing In 'B' Group This Day, The Court Made The
Following:
 Order

The petitioner has sought for a direction to acquire the land in Sy.No.567/1 belonging to him and situate at Srinivas Saradagi village, Kalaburagi Taluk and District and to pay compensation as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner contends that he is the owner of the aforesaid land and a road ran through Srinivas Saradagi village to Khaja Kotnur village.
He contends that the respondent Nos.2 to 6 were forming a road in Sy.No.567/1, which was earlier a katcha village road.
He has contended that the respondent Nos.2 to 4 have encroached upon the land of the petitioner and were forming a 150 feet National Highway.
The petitioner contends that he immediately approached the respondent Nos.2 to 4 requesting them to remove the encroachment on his land.
However, his representations were not considered.

The petitioner contends that he got his land surveyed to measure the area of the road Alisab vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5879432/
2 passing through his land in Sy.No.567/1, and the area which was unauthorisedly encroached upon.

entities.text: Alisab vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was found that the an area measuring 80 feet North to South running from Sannur to Srinivas Saradagi was acquired and therefore, his entire land was used up for the purpose of laying a road.
He then filed a representation requesting the respondents to acquire his land and to pay compensation as provided in law.

The respondent No.4 replied to the representation claiming that the land lay within the jurisdiction of the Sub-Division of Humnabad and therefore, NC:
2024:KHC-K:3530 directed the petitioner to contact respondent No.5.
The petitioner then made a representation to respondent No.5, who replied to the petitioner claiming that the land of the petitioner was not utilized by the respondent No.5.

It was also mentioned that the National Highways Authority was developing the road from 21 to 31 kilometer by widening it to 15 meters on either side from the center of the road and that there was no encroachment by the National Highway.
The petitioner therefore, has approached this Court seeking for the aforementioned reliefs.

3. The petition is opposed by the respondent No.5 who filed a detailed statement of objections contending that the road between Srinivas Saradagi to Khaja Kotnur village is a major district road and as per the Government Order dated 09.10.1998, 25 meters from the center of the road belongs to the Public Works Department.

It is contended that the respondent No.5 has undertaken the project within 25 meters from the centerline on either side and therefore, the respondent No.5 has not encroached into any land belonging to the petitioner.
As such, the question of acquisition of land belonging to the petitioner does not arise.

It is contended that NC: 2024:KHC-K:3530 the Government of India vide its Order dated 02.11.2016 had granted an administrative and financial sanction for reconstruction of Major District Road under Phase - I of Central Road Fund Scheme at an estimated cost of Rs.8 crores.

Further, it is claimed that the Chief Engineer, National Highways,
Bengaluru has granted a technical sanction to take up reconstruction work through contractor vide Work Order dated 11.12.2017.
Thus, it is contended that the road is developed for the public benefit and is the only access to Kalaburagi Airport.
It is further contended that the petitioner had not produced any document to show what was the measurement of the property, width of the road after development etc.,
It is also contended that the petitioner failed to produce any document to establish the area of land encroached into by the respondent No.5.
With these and other contentions, the respondent No.5 contended that the petitioner is not entitled to any of the reliefs sought for.

4. This Court in W.P.No.200963/2018 c/w W.P.No.200663/2018 (D.D. 23.12.2020) had held that the land lying within the building line or control line is also to be acquired in accordance with law and that the State Highways NC: 2024:KHC-K:3530 Authorities under the Karnataka State Highways Act cannot contend that the land lying within the control line belongs exclusively to the State Government.

In the case on hand too, the respondent No.5 has contended that it has developed road on either side of the existing road and has widened the existing road by 25 meters on either side from the central line.
This only indicated that the respondents were developing the existing road within the control line.
Therefore, the question is the extent of land in Sy.No.567/1 belonging to the petitioner that was used up for such development.
If the land of the petitioner lay within the control line then, he was undoubtedly entitled to be compensated by the respondents for using up his portion of the land for the development of the road.

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, without affirmatively answering the question, whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation or not, this petition is allowed.

A mandamus is issued to the respondent No.5 to measure and fix the boundaries of the land of the petitioner based on the survey records and thereafter, identify the area of the land used up in Sy.No.567/1 for the purpose of widening the road and then, award suitable compensation as is provided in law.
It is made NC: 2024:KHC-K:3530 clear that if the land of the petitioner is not used for the development of the road, then the petitioner would not be entitled to any benefit.
6. The respondent No.5 shall comply with the aforesaid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Order.
